apps/api/app/repositories/story.py.purpose: create() computes contentHash, SELECTs an existing row with the same (userId, contentHash) and returns it instead of inserting a duplicate; update() recomputes the hash when any STAR field changes; read paths switched to a new _READ_COLUMNS list that omits contentHash.
risks: HIGH (API-3) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE by code read + call-site grep] apps/api/app/repositories/story.py update() appends '"contentHash" = %s' to the UPDATE SET clause but NEVER calls ensure_story_dedup_column(). grep -rn 'ensure_story_dedup_column' apps/api/ returns exactly two call sites: the def in db.py:338 and ONE invocation at story.py:31 (create only). The module-level _story_dedup_column_ready guard is per-process, so in a freshly restarted api process whose first StoryEntry operation is a PUT /stories/{id} carrying a STAR field, the column has never been ensured. [INFERRED] Production schema 'aether' has never run this DDL (prod runs pre-WIP code per EXTERNAL-CLIENT-ACCESS-FIX-2026-07-29.md OBS-EXT-004), so that PUT raises psycopg2 UndefinedColumn -> HTTP 500. Not caught by tests because the shared aether_test schema already has the column once any create-path test has run.

MED (API-4) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] Response-shape inconsistency and internal-value leak. story.py:5-8 _COLUMNS (used by the INSERT ... RETURNING) INCLUDES contentHash; the dedup-hit branch re-SELECTs with _READ_COLUMNS which EXCLUDES it. apps/api/app/routers/stories.py:144-146 create_story is annotated '-> dict[str, Any]' with NO response_model, so FastAPI serializes the repository dict verbatim. Consequence: POST /stories returns the raw internal sha256 on a first insert and omits the field entirely on a dedup hit — two different response shapes from one endpoint, one of them exposing an internal dedup token.

LOW (API-5) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] File no longer ends with a newline (xxd of the last 30 bytes ends '...return deleted > 0' with no 0x0a; git diff reports '\ No newline at end of file'). A classic interrupted-edit marker, and a diff-noise/lint regression.
notes: The create() dedup logic itself is correct and proven by 6 green tests; the incompleteness is confined to update(), the response shape, and EOF hygiene.

apps/api/app/routers/agents.py.purpose: Adds 'except FabricationError' and 'except StructuralError' handlers to _execute_reserved_run so a guard rejection is recorded as an honest COMPLETED degrade (coverLetterUnavailable) rather than a red 'failed' Activity row (GAP-P4-002).
risks: BLOCKER (API-1) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE, runtime traceback] apps/api/app/routers/agents.py:785 'except FabricationError as exc:' and :805 'except StructuralError as exc:' reference names that are NEVER bound at module scope. grep over agents.py shows the ONLY imports of these symbols are FUNCTION-LOCAL, at line 1611 and line 1754 ('from app.agents.cover_letter_agent import FabricationError, StructuralError'), neither of which is in scope inside _execute_reserved_run. The module header (agents.py:8-57) imports nothing from app.agents.cover_letter_agent.

BLOCKER (API-1, blast radius) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] Python evaluates except-clause expressions in order at raise time. The chain in _execute_reserved_run is: HTTPException -> NoChangesApplied -> FabricationError(UNDEFINED) -> StructuralError(UNDEFINED) -> QuotaExhaustedError -> LLMUnavailableError -> Exception. Therefore EVERY exception that is not HTTPException and not NoChangesApplied now dies on a NameError BEFORE reaching its intended handler. Concretely: (a) runs.finish(run_id, 'failed', ...) never executes, leaving the AgentRun audit row orphaned in 'running' forever; (b) _refund_once() never executes, so a PAYING USER'S RESERVED RUN IS NEVER REFUNDED after a failure — a direct billing defect; (c) LLMUnavailableError no longer maps to a clean 503 and QuotaExhaustedError no longer maps to 429 — both surface as an opaque 500. This is precisely the honest-error-state and no-silent-failure standard being violated, and it is a revenue-affecting regression.

BLOCKER (API-1, proof) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] Two PRE-EXISTING, UNTOUCHED tests fail on this working tree: 'flock /tmp/aether-pytest.lock scripts/run-tests.sh tests/test_ml_agents_err_001_obs.py tests/test_llm_resilience.py -q' -> '2 failed, 29 passed'. Both failures are tests/test_llm_resilience.py::TestRouter503Mapping::test_tailor_returns_503_not_500_when_llm_unavailable and ::test_failed_run_is_audited. Captured traceback: '>       except FabricationError as exc:' / 'E       NameError: name FabricationError is not defined' / 'app/routers/agents.py:785: NameError'. test_llm_resilience.py is NOT in the modified-file set, so the regression is unambiguously attributable to this WIP hunk.

HIGH (API-2) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] Zero test coverage for the intended new behaviour. No test asserts that a FabricationError or StructuralError produces status='completed' with coverLetterUnavailable=true on the AgentRun row. The TDD standard (failing-before evidence, legible) is entirely unmet for the branch's namesake change.

MED (API-6) — [INFERRED] The handler records status='completed' with cost_usd=0.0 AND calls _refund_once() AND re-raises. On the async path _execute_reserved_run is invoked with manage_quota=False (agents.py:717-724 docstring) so _refund_once() is a no-op and the worker refunds after its first-terminal-wins transition — but the re-raise now also propagates past a handler that already wrote a terminal 'completed' status, so the async worker may write a SECOND terminal transition for the same run. Unproven either way, and untested. Needs a probe before this handler ships.

LOW (API-7) — [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] 'honest_output: dict[str, Any]' is re-annotated in two sibling except blocks within a scope that already assigns an unannotated 'honest_output' in the NoChangesApplied handler. Legal at runtime; a mypy redefinition complaint.
notes: [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] The attribute accesses themselves are correct: apps/api/app/agents/cover_letter_agent.py:1043-1046 defines FabricationError.flagged and :1049-1056 defines StructuralError.issues. The defect is purely the missing module-level import — but its consequence is severe and unbounded.

[VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] The inline comment claims the reason string is 'NEVER verbatim LLM output, zero PII risk'. str(exc.flagged) is a list of guard-extracted entity strings lifted FROM the model draft (e.g. ['origination']); calling that 'never verbatim LLM output' is an overstatement. Low risk in practice, but the comment asserts more than the code guarantees.

coherenceAssessment: The tree is SIX independent workstreams sharing one working directory, not one coherent change. Only the story-dedup cluster (db.py + dedup.py + story.py + test_story_dedup.py) has genuine internal coupling; every other file is independent of every other. Two of the six workstreams contain defects that are individually sufficient to block a commit, and the branch's own namesake workstream (GAP-P4-002 in agents.py) is the single most broken thing in the tree.

recommendationDetail.headline: REVERT the tree as it stands. Do NOT commit it, and do NOT restart aether-api until at minimum apps/api/app/routers/agents.py and apps/api/app/repositories/story.py are reverted.
recommendationDetail.rationale: COMMIT-AS-IS is disqualified outright by API-1 (proven NameError breaking refunds and the failure audit trail for paying users) and WEB-1 (proven false user-facing metric copy). COMPLETE-AND-COMMIT is rejected as a single action because completing this tree is not a bug-fix exercise: it requires an owner pricing ruling (WEB-3), an ADR-level reversal or abandonment of documented data-consistency ruling MV-analytics-005 (WEB-1), and an unresolved async double-terminal-transition design question (API-6). None of those can be closed by a fixer, and the api deploy blocked behind this decision (QA-RES-001, the Gmail credential-cache fix) should not wait on them. Reverting the four api files unblocks aether-api restart IMMEDIATELY and costs nothing that cannot be re-landed cleanly.

apiRestartSafeExplanation: [VERIFIED-WITH-FRESH-EVIDENCE] NO. Restarting aether-api against this tree loads apps/api/app/routers/agents.py with two undefined-name except clauses at lines 785 and 805. From that moment, every agent-run failure that is not an HTTPException or NoChangesApplied raises NameError instead of its handler: the AgentRun row is never finished (orphaned 'running' forever), the reserved run is NEVER REFUNDED to a paying user, LLM outages return 500 instead of 503, and quota exhaustion returns 500 instead of 429. Proven, not theorised — two untouched pre-existing tests fail with the exact traceback 'NameError: name FabricationError is not defined / app/routers/agents.py:785'. A second, independent restart hazard exists in apps/api/app/repositories/story.py: update() writes "contentHash" without ever calling ensure_story_dedup_column(), and production's aether schema has never had that column, so the first PUT /stories/{id} carrying a STAR field in a fresh process returns 500.
apiRestartSafeAfterRevertExplanation: [INFERRED] Reverting the four api-side files (app/db.py, app/repositories/story.py, app/routers/agents.py, app/services/dedup.py) returns the api tree to HEAD 5f0af49, which is the code family production has been running healthily. tests/test_llm_resilience.py::TestRouter503Mapping should then pass again — re-run it as the restart gate before touching the service.
reasoning: Three independent, individually-blocking defects, each proven with fresh command output rather than inference. (1) apps/api/app/routers/agents.py:785 and :805 catch FabricationError and StructuralError, which are bound nowhere at module scope — the only imports are function-local at lines 1611 and 1754. Because Python evaluates except expressions in order at raise time, this makes every handler BELOW them unreachable, so failed agent runs are neither audited nor refunded; two untouched pre-existing tests now fail with 'NameError: name FabricationError is not defined'. This is a revenue-affecting billing regression that arms itself on the next api restart or VM reboot. (2) apps/web/src/app/dashboard/analytics/page.tsx now tells users the Applications card shows 'distinct jobs submitted to an employer ... drafts in progress are excluded', while apps/api/app/routers/analytics.py:631 demonstrably feeds it the drafts-INCLUSIVE total — proven by the green apps/api/tests/test_analytics.py:230-232 which seeds 3 drafts + 4 submitted and asserts the card shows 7. The accompanying test edit asserts the false string, converting the falsehood into a protected regression. On a branch named 'remove fabricated origination activity', this ADDS a fabricated claim and silently reverses documented ruling MV-analytics-005 with no ADR. (3) apps/api/app/repositories/story.py update() writes the new contentHash column without ever ensuring it exists, a latent 500 on a production schema that has never seen the DDL. Against those, the tree contains real value — the story-dedup cluster is 6/6 green and its lazy DDL correctly mirrors the ensure_job_dedup_columns/ADR-TR-1 precedent, and the MarketPulse honest-unavailable state is exemplary — but that value is separable and re-landable, whereas the risk is not containable in a single commit. Completing the tree in place is additionally impossible without decisions no fixer owns: an owner pricing ruling on the /dashboard/email paywall exemption, an ADR on the analytics metric semantics, and a design answer on async double-terminal transitions. Reverting the four api files is therefore the fastest and safest path: it makes aether-api restart-safe within minutes and unblocks the queued Gmail credential-cache deploy (QA-RES-001), while each surviving workstream re-lands on its own merits with the tests it currently lacks.
verdictSummary: FAIL — this tree must not be committed and aether-api must not be restarted against it.
